pue.boundary: OCI external AI compute, matched data-center total and IT energy
pue.basis: CDP describes invoice-based site IT power and PUE inputs but withholds matched site values/weights. 2020 best-case1.15 is historical reference only. No transferable operational low/base/high can be defended.

model.revenue_scope: External AI-attributable portion of CPU/GPU infrastructure after hardware/non-compute adjustment; not whole OCI
model.capacity_time_basis: 92-day quarter; sum(active AI IT MW * active days)/92 and sum(active AI IT MW * active days * physical utilization)/92. Missing initial fleet and activation dates prevent reconstruction.

formulas.facility_sensitivity: For matched fixed average facility MW, revenue and physical utilization: output = annualized_AI_revenue*PUE/(average_AI_facility_MW*physical_utilization)/1e6. Higher PUE raises this quotient by shrinking the IT denominator, not by improving efficiency.
formulas.IT_sensitivity: With a reported IT boundary, omit PUE. At fixed numerator and active IT MW, output varies inversely with physical utilization.
formulas.chips_per_IT_MW: 1000 / all-in IT kW per GPU including allocated CPU, networking and storage; GPU TDP alone insufficient. Facility conversion needs matched operational PUE.
formulas.jevons: For a supported price decline d and fixed revenue, required volume growth=d/(1-d); no scoped d available.

assumptions.basis: Quarterly run-rate convention only; not full-year guidance.
No physical definition/weights for97.9% issuer claim; no fabricated low/base/high.
Historical best site and generation/IT ratios excluded. Need same-period site energy weights.

structured_deals.economic_effect: Q1 $11.363B financing prepayments support cash funding; significant financing component creates interest expense over performance. Majority Q1 RPO growth involves prepaid or customer hardware. Customer-owned hardware can reduce Oracle procurement burden but does not erase site leases, operating costs or delivery liability.

$288B uncommenced commitments at Aug31, up net$28B from May31; expected Q2FY27-FY29 commencements with15-19year terms. Separate from commenced operating$48.050B and finance$15.195B undiscounted payments and their$34.621B/$9.185B PV liabilities; do not double count.

$34.150B long-term unconditional obligations mix cloud components and power. Not pure PPA balance. Annual$13.309B primarily power and subsequent$19B hardware are earlier observations, not independent additions to August aggregate.
141M common shares issued for$19.909B net proceeds. June23 supplement adds agents to same$20B program, not a second authorization. Funding supports liquidity but dilutes equity.
May31 maximum$3.3B guarantee for debt due September2026. Current payoff/refinancing/draw unknown. Do not assume guarantee disappeared because August-quarter disclosure lacks repeat text.

July22,2025 agreement covers4.5GW additional development. Capacity, chip and funding targets are forward commitments, not billable average IT MW; detailed pricing, take-or-pay and guarantees unavailable.

May2025$15B project JV and1.2GW plan are project financing/facility capacity. September10 Oracle management claims618MW/six buildings delivered; neither figure supplies dated IT activation history. JV funding is not Oracle compute revenue and accounting/recourse details not established.

April27 plan up to2.45GW installed fuel-cell generation, Oracle paying energy costs. Generation rating is not IT MW/PUE. October12 NMED still displays permit-process stay; neither cancellation nor default established. September secondary loan marks not refreshed.

findings: Exact Q1 IaaS$7.388B supersedes rounded$7.4B. Deck CPU/GPU$6.5B is a narrower recognized-revenue subtotal excluding database, but still cannot support AI revenue per effective MW.

Management reports97.9% AI infrastructure utilization and20% average renewal/resale premium for GPUs renewing inQ1. This is strongest disconfirming evidence against indiscriminate near-term GPU price-collapse assumptions; physical definitions and cohort mix remain unknown.

Financing prepayments are not cost-free capital: Note1 requires interest expense. Analytical OCF less selected prepayments is$11.740B and cash-capex gap$16.759B, versus reportedFCF deficit$5.396B. Equity proceeds and$37.077B cash/securities offset an immediate-liquidity-stress interpretation.
PUE has an identifiable disclosure route—site invoices used by Oracle—but no public matching site inputs. The2020 as-low-as1.15 claim does not justify selecting a current fleet PUE.
Permit stay remains visibleOctober12; current guarantee outcome and loan market marks remain unresolved. Delivery claims should be dated and distinguished from energized/accepted IT capacity.
gaps: CPU/GPU subtotal is not AI-only: attributable external AI recognized revenue and hardware/non-compute pass-through adjustments remain undisclosed.

No beginning active AI IT-MW fleet, dated activation cohorts, hardware generation inventory or matched physical utilization: 850MW additions and >300,000 delivered GPUs cannot reconstruct quarter-average active capacity or chips per IT MW.
No same-period AI-fleet total/IT energy or published invoice-level site PUE and IT-energy weights. Historical best-case1.15 is not a defensible operational fleet range.

Full prepayment/BYOH agreements, effective financing rates, price resets, acceptance/delivery remedies, GPU title, replacement/residual-value obligations and project-specific take-or-pay rights are unavailable.

The May31 up-to$3.3B lessor guarantee covered borrowing due September2026; reviewed August31 filing and September14 8-K do not establish payoff, refinancing, draw or continued guarantee exposure after maturity.

Project-level debt/PPA agreements, SPV/VIE consolidation analysis, guarantees, current Jupiter loan trading indications, signed court order and final permit disposition remain unverified. September secondary prices are not October12 quotes.
No attributable token/task price-volume series or model mix to connect proprietary/open inference revenue to exact Jevons break-even; renewal premium is not token price deflation.
